answer: I'd like to talk about something I've held onto since I was about ten years old. Something I have kept for many years is a childhood diary that I started writing when I was quite young. It's a thick notebook with a faded cartoon cover, full of my untidy handwriting, little drawings and even a few pressed flowers. I have held onto it for well over a decade now, moving it carefully from one flat to another whenever my family moved. These days it lives in a drawer in my desk. It contains my youthful thoughts, dreams and daily events, which are often [[amusing]] to read back now. There's one entry where I announced very seriously that I would become a famous cricketer, and another describing an argument with my younger sister over the last piece of a mango. I have kept it because it is a genuine [[time capsule]] of who I once was. Whenever I flick through it, I feel a wave of [[nostalgia]] for a simpler time in my life. What makes it so precious is that no amount of money could recreate those honest, [[unfiltered]] memories. It is fascinating, and occasionally [[embarrassing]], to see how much my perspective has changed. Honestly, I think keeping such personal records is genuinely valuable. It reminds me of how far I have come and grounds me in my own history. I fully intend to keep it for the rest of my life; it is far too [[meaningful]] to ever throw away.

followUps.q: Do you still keep a diary now?
followUps.answer: Not a daily one, sadly. Life got busier, but I still jot down my thoughts in a notebook now and then, especially after important events, because I know I'll enjoy [[looking back on]] them later.

followUps.q: Would you let anyone read your old diary?
followUps.answer: Only my younger sister, and only certain pages. Some entries are far too embarrassing, although we had a good laugh when she found the one about our argument over the mango.
